currentContext.business: The Company manufactures biodiesel - a renewable, biodegradable fuel produced by transesterification of vegetable oils, waste oils, animal fats, tallow and used cooking oil - at two plants, at Sirohi (Rajasthan) and Anand (Gujarat), and sells it to Oil Marketing Companies for blending into diesel and speed-diesel and to bulk buyers such as transport contractors, mining companies and industries in the plants' vicinity. Alongside biodiesel it sells Veg Ester (semi-finished biodiesel, sold on to other processing units) and crude glycerine, the by-product of transesterification, which it has begun refining on site into graded glycerin for food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic and carpet-manufacturing uses. Incorporated in December 2016 as a biofuel trader, it built its first plant in 2019, listed on NSE Emerge in November 2021 and migrated to the NSE and BSE Main Boards during FY 2025-26.

Bio-Diesel: Biodiesel (B100 / neat biodiesel; mono alkyl ester) produced by transesterification of vegetable oil, animal fats, tallow and used cooking oil
Biodiesel supplied to OMCs for blending in diesel and premium-category speed-diesel
Biodiesel supplied to bulk buyers - transport contractors, mining companies and industries in the vicinity of the plants
Veg Ester-Semi Finished: Veg Ester - semi-finished biodiesel that, with further processing, is converted into biodiesel; sold to other processing units for generation of biodiesel
Crude Glycerin: Crude glycerin - by-product of the transesterification reaction; 'the production of 100 litres of biodiesel yields about 14 litres of crude glycerin'
Refined glycerin in different grades, produced by further refining crude glycerin in an on-site processing plant, for food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications
Carbon credits: Carbon credits registered and issued under Verra; 57,874 carbon credits accumulated for the period September 15, 2020 to March 31, 2022

currentContext.expansion: Kotyark runs two manufacturing facilities - Sirohi (Rajasthan), its first plant, built in 2019, and Anand (Gujarat). The one named expansion project in the routed text is the Rajasthan debottlenecking/expansion: 'Last year the Company expanded the biodiesel production capacity at its Rajasthan facility from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, significantly strengthening its manufacturing capabilities. Consequently, the Company's total installed annual production capacity increased to approximately 4,80,000 KL of biodiesel and 63,000 KL of crude glycerine.' The AR gives no commissioning date, no cost and no as-of date for this project, and 'Last year' is undated - in an FY 2025-26 report it may mean FY 2024-25 or may be a paragraph carried over from the prior year's AR; nothing was inferred. The second project is a downstream one: the Company 'took a significant step forward by installing a glycerin processing pilot plant with a capacity of 210 KL per day at its Sirohi facility', supporting its move from selling crude glycerine to refining it on site into graded glycerin (this sentence reaches only the risks_esg bundle - the copy of the same Corporate Overview spread routed to capex_expansion is truncated before it). Anand has no separately stated capacity. Beyond these, management describes no new plant, line, brownfield or greenfield project and no capex programme: forward intent is expressed only as utilising the enlarged base - 'improving operational efficiency, increasing capacity utilisation, strengthening its raw material sourcing network and expanding its participation in tenders issued by Oil Marketing Companies' - plus generic intent to expand market presence, improve manufacturing efficiencies and adopt advanced technologies while 'building a sustainable, integrated and scalable green energy platform'. The Company also completed a listing-status change during FY 2025-26, migrating its shares from the NSE Emerge Platform to the Main Board of both NSE and BSE.

risks.note: 'Availability and prices of feedstocks such as used cooking oil and other renewable raw materials may fluctuate due to market dynamics, impacting production costs and margins.' This is the Company's first-listed risk and is structural: biodiesel economics are a spread between a volatile waste/vegetable-oil input and an OMC-set output price. The multi-feedstock platform (approximately 10-15 feedstocks) is the stated mitigant, giving substitution ability but not price protection.

risks.risk: Customer concentration on Oil Marketing Companies
risks.note: 'A significant portion of revenue comes from Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), potentially exposing the Company to risks associated with reliance on a limited customer base.' The AR names no other channel of comparable size beyond local bulk buyers, so a small set of state-linked buyers effectively sets both volume and price.

risks.risk: Dependence on OMC procurement programmes and tender/indent timing
risks.note: 'Procurement programmes and tender schedules of Oil Marketing Companies play an important role in the biodiesel market. Changes in procurement volumes or timelines may affect sales performance.' This risk materialised in FY26: management states that 'delays in the issuance of Purchase Orders (POs) and Indents despite sizable tender allocations led to elevated inventory levels and impacted short-term margins' - i.e. an allocation win does not convert to revenue on the Company's own timetable, and the shortfall lands in working capital.

'The biofuel industry is influenced by Government policies relating to procurement, blending programmes, taxation and environmental regulations. Any significant changes in these policies may impact business operations.' The entire demand thesis rests on the National Policy on Biofuels and the blending trajectory - the AR itself notes blending is currently below 1% against a Government goal of 5% by 2030 - so policy slippage removes the growth driver rather than merely delaying it.

risks.risk: Commodity and energy price risk - biodiesel's competitiveness versus diesel
risks.note: 'Fluctuations in crude oil prices and energy costs may influence the competitiveness of biodiesel compared to conventional fuels and affect overall industry dynamics.' Bulk-buyer demand is explicitly a price-arbitrage proposition - 'Traditionally, biodiesel trades cheaper than diesel in India, offering bulk buyers an opportunity to cut costs' - so a fall in crude erodes the discretionary, non-OMC part of the book.

risks.risk: Operational and supply-chain risk at the manufacturing sites
risks.note: 'Manufacturing operations are exposed to risks associated with plant operations, equipment reliability, utilities, logistics and supply chain disruptions.' With only two plants - Sirohi (Rajasthan) and Anand (Gujarat) - and the enlarged capacity concentrated at Sirohi, an outage at a single site is a company-level event. The stated mitigation is strengthened operational processes and preventive maintenance systems.

risks.risk: Utilisation risk on the enlarged capacity base
risks.note: Structural rather than labelled: the Company has taken Rajasthan biodiesel capacity from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD and total installed annual capacity to approximately 4,80,000 KL, while naming 'increasing capacity utilisation' as a continuing focus and disclosing no utilisation percentage or production volume anywhere in the routed text. Fixed-cost absorption therefore depends on OMC offtake the Company does not control.

Structural rather than labelled: 'Biodiesel forms the core of Kotyark's product portfolio.' The routed text describes no segment other than biodiesel and its by-products (Veg Ester semi-finished and crude/refined glycerine), and the glycerin refining step is still at pilot scale (a 210 KL/day pilot plant at Sirohi), so the diversification is real but early.
